title: Hyphens and semicolons typed in a line are carried as written
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Tech Story is on (Settings, then the Work Orders tab).
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with two labor lines: line 1 titled "Replace tie rod - passenger side" with the description "excessive play - customer waiting", and line 2 titled "Replace tie rod" with the description "excessive play; also checked the drag link".
  • Have line 1 completed with the tech story "Torqued to 74 ft-lb, alignment set", line 2 completed with the tech story "Drag link within spec", and work order 1 completed and invoiced today as invoice A.
  • Use Google Sheets (File, then Import, then Upload) to open downloaded files, so accented letters and character counts read correctly.
  • Start on Reports, then Export Reports in the Reports left menu, with the Export Report dialog open.
custom_steps:
1. Pick Customer Invoice in the Report Name list.
  2. Set the date range to today.
  3. Click Download.
  4. Open the downloaded file in Google Sheets.
  5. In an empty cell, enter =LEN() with line 1's ItemDescription cell inside the brackets.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer Invoice is picked in Report Name.

Step 2:

  • The date range shows today's date.

Step 3:

  • A Customer Invoice file downloads.

Step 4:

  • In line 1's row (work order 1's invoice A) the ItemDescription cell reads exactly "Replace tie rod - passenger side - excessive play - customer waiting - Torqued to 74 ft-lb, alignment set".
  • In line 2's row the ItemDescription cell reads exactly "Replace tie rod - excessive play; also checked the drag link - Drag link within spec".
  • The hyphens and the semicolon typed inside the values are kept, and nothing is put in quotes or marked with extra characters such as a backslash.

Step 5:

  • The cell shows 105 (32 + 3 + 33 + 3 + 34 = 105): nothing was added or removed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 16 (27 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks)

  • S3-R9: “A title, a description or a narrative that itself contains a hyphen, including a spaced hyphen, is carried as written. The separator is not escaped and the text is not quoted, so a reader cannot always tell our separator from theirs. This is accepted deliberately: the alternative is printing a field name to mark the join, which is the thing being removed.”
  • S3-R9a: “A semicolon typed inside any of the three values is ordinary punctuation and is carried through untouched. It was ambiguous only while the semicolon was the separator.”
  • S3-R8: “The values themselves are unchanged. Nothing is trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped that is not trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped today, other than the shortening described in S3-R7 and the removal of spaces and line breaks at the very end of the whole line (S3-R3), and the apostrophe in S3-R8a.”
  • S3-R5: “The technician's narrative is the third and last segment. It carries no label of any kind, and no semicolon appears anywhere in the line text. The reasoning is in §2.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.

The design's own words:

  • “Carried as written. Nothing is escaped or quoted, so a reader cannot tell our separator from theirs. This is the cost of the choice and it is accepted deliberately: the alternative is printing a field name to mark the join, which is the thing two customers asked us to stop doing.”
  • “With the semicolon gone, a typed semicolon is ordinary punctuation and carries through untouched.”
